one_liner: Direct-to-consumer skincare brand selling through its own site and marketplaces
business_model: Direct-to-consumer skincare brand selling through its own site and marketplaces. Roughly 18 months old, a few thousand monthly orders, strong Instagram presence.

claims.text: Direct-to-consumer skincare brand selling through its own site and marketplaces. Roughly 18 months old, a few thousand monthly orders, strong Instagram presence.

Risks recorded by the fund: Customer acquisition cost rising month on month; roughly two thirds of orders from paid social. Repeat rate not tracked. Product made by a single contract manufacturer. Category is crowded with better-funded incumbents.

Partner assessment of founders from the meeting: Anika Rao, solo founder, formerly a brand manager at a large FMCG company. Articulate, polished, and clearly good at brand and creative. She was candid that she had never owned a P&L and had no co-founder covering operations or supply chain. In the call she answered unit-economics questions with channel-level averages, not cohort data. Our read: a strong marketer, not yet a business builder, and unaware of the gap.
